newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Tuesday on profit-taking by retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,174 yuan ($383), losing 76 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 3,200 yuan and hit a low of 3,170 yuan per tonne.
November lost nine to 3,146 yuan, the January 1998 contract rose 38 to 3,140 and March fell eight to 3,132 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 19,900 tonnes from 21,900 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mostly lower and fell further for most of the session, traders said.
"Profit-taking from retail investors dominated today's trading after gains over the past few days," one trader said.
"Technical charts show a downward trend, and that has encouraged longs to cover their positions," said another trader.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move slightly down in the next few days.
